key_insight: A differentiable overlapping Schwarz solver couples near-wall and bulk transport, enabling inverse modeling of thin boundary layers with coarser meshes.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce computational costs when inferring unknown parameters in high-Péclet-number transport with steep near-wall gradients.
method: Split near-wall and bulk physics using perturbation theory and overlapping Schwarz coupling.
Discretize both subproblems with finite elements and use adjoint sensitivities while enforcing physics as hard constraints.
Compare LLM-driven parameter updates with an agentic workflow that expands a functional basis under a prescribed admission policy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower computational cost than a single-domain formulation and greater agentic AI benefit for functional-basis unknowns than nodal fields, without quantitative metrics.
watch_item: Agentic optimization benefits may depend on the unknown's representation and the policy governing basis-function admission.
paper_title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
